question.problem:
The table below gives the values of a continuous function $f(x)$ over the closed interval $[2,8]$ with a regular step size.

| $x$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $-3$ | $5$ | $k$ | $1$ |

If the left Riemann sum approximation of the area under the curve $y=f(x)$ with $3$ subintervals defined by the given points has a value of $18$, then what must be the value of $k?$ 

$\,\,k=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The area $A$ can be approximated using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈(\overset{\text{heights}}{\overset{⏞}{f({x}_{0})+f({x}_{1})+f({x}_{2})}})\cdot \,\,{{Δx}_{⏟}}_{\text{ }\text{width}} \\  & =(f(2)+f(4)+f(6))\cdot Δx.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the points are $2,4,6,8$ with three subintervals, the step size is

$$
Δx=\frac{8-2}{3}=2.
$$

So, we now set up a table with the values of $f(x)$ at each left-endpoint:

| $x$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $-3$ | $5$ | $k$ |

So, we obtain the following approximation to the area:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ≈((-3)+5+k)\cdot 2 \\  & =(2+k)\cdot 2 \\  & =4+2k.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since we are given that $A=18$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}4+2k & =18 \\ 2k & =14 \\ k & =7.\end{aligned}
$$
